name: Hoi An
provinceNote: Hoi An was in Quang Nam, which merged into Da Nang in 2025. Search and book it as Hoi An.
summary: Sleep in Hoi An when you want the timber streets after dark, the covered bridge at the west end, and the river the houses back onto. Sleep in Da Nang when the morning is the beach. The old town is a walk. The sightseeing fee is check on arrival.
getThere: Da Nang International Airport (DAD), then the road south. The ancient town is about 30 km southeast of Da Nang city. The minutes are check on arrival.
seoTitle: Hoi An travel guide — timber streets and the bridge
seoDescription: The ancient town is about 30 km southeast of Da Nang. From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND a building. Floods are usual in September to November.
intro: The street is a tight row of tiled timber shophouses, with the covered wooden bridge at the west end and the river the houses back onto. Walk it in the morning, then again after the shops thin, inside the pedestrian hours the heritage centre printed in January 2026: 09:00–21:30 in summer and 09:00–21:00 in winter. The notice does not say which months those words cover.

Sleep in the lanes just off that core when the evening is the trip. Sleep in Da Nang when the morning is the beach. An Bang is the Hoi An swim, a villa and homestay base in what is now Hoi An Tây. The ride from the old town is check on arrival. Cửa Đại’s erosion is serious, and the same coast article says An Bang and Tân Thành are also threatened.

The sightseeing fee is check on arrival. From 10 August 2026, Da Nang’s resolution sets 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for a Vietnamese and a foreign visitor. The heritage centre’s notices of 26 January 2026 and 16 March 2026 still describe combination tickets: 80,000 VND for the streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works, and 120,000 VND when a museum and three other works are added. A May 2026 article says the town is an open neighbourhood and many people walk in without a ticket, and it counts those prices as four works and six. Ask which rule the desk is using that day.
gettingAround: The ancient town is about 30 km southeast of Da Nang city. The minutes from the airport are check on arrival. From the Marble Mountains, the coastal road along Trường Sa–Lạc Long Quân is about 30 minutes. The rail stop is Ga Đà Nẵng, then the road south. The station address and those minutes are check on arrival.

Route 02 runs from Đà Nẵng central station through the Hoi An bus station to the inland-waterway parking at Cửa Đại, from 05:30 to 18:00, every 20–30 minutes. The operator’s December 2025 page gives a fare band of 8,000–30,000 VND, with pupils and students at 8,000 VND. A July 2025 report gives 8,000–48,000 VND across route 02 and route 21. The price at the Hoi An stop, and the ride time, are check on arrival.

Inside the ancient town, walk. The January 2026 notice prints old-town pedestrian hours of 09:00–21:30 in summer and 09:00–21:00 in winter, and Phan Châu Trinh from 17:30 to 21:30 in summer and to 21:00 in winter, between Nguyễn Huệ and Cao Hồng Lãnh. A 2023 notice described a later 15:00 start. The January 2026 notice still prints 17:30. Whether that afternoon start is in force is check on arrival. A bicycle or a ride is the way to An Bang and to Trà Quế, about 2.5 km north on the heritage page and about 2 km northeast on the national tourism page. The minutes are check on arrival.

eat: Cao lầu is tossed while it is hot. People here call it bánh. White rose dumplings are a small warm plate. Chicken rice is the lunch when you want a plate instead of noodles. Bánh mì is the morning stall in the old town.
The food hall is inside Chợ Hội An. The night market is on Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng. Hours for both are check on arrival.
interestsBody: Dining is cao lầu tossed while it is hot, white rose dumplings warm, and chicken rice when you want a plate. Mì Quảng is the neighbor’s bowl. The food guide is the first stop.
The night is the timber streets inside the pedestrian hours, and the covered bridge at the west end. That is the reason to sleep here.
Merchant houses such as Tấn Ký are the inside of the street: a shop at the front and the river at the back. The ground floor is the visit.
The assembly halls are the Hoa merchant halls. Quảng Đông is the dragon court. Phúc Kiến is the long hall on Trần Phú. Chùa Ông is at 24 Trần Phú.
The museums are a morning hour: trade ceramics at 80 Trần Phú, Sa Huỳnh pottery at 149 Trần Phú, and the folk-culture house at 33 Nguyễn Thái Học.
Trà Quế is the herb beds about 2.5 km north on the heritage page, and about 2 km northeast on the national tourism page. The greens go into cao lầu.
Kim Bồng is the carpentry village across the river. Thanh Hà is the pottery west of town. Crossing minutes and the ride are check on arrival.
An Bang is the swim and the villa stay, now in Hoi An Tây. Cửa Đại’s erosion is serious, and the same coast article says this beach is threatened too. The ride from the old town is check on arrival.
Cẩm Thanh is the basket-boat hour in the nipa water, about 3 km out on the 2022 article. From 10 August 2026 the entry is 30,000 VND. The boat price is check on arrival.
Resort living is Cua Dai when you want a pool morning and the old town at night.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Clay from Thanh Hà and carved wood from Kim Bồng. The silk village on the 2018 list has no licensed photograph, so it stays in the text.

blocks.heading: Thanh Hà clay
paragraphs: The craft index places Thanh Hà in khối Nam Diêu, Thanh Hà ward, 3 kilometres west-southwest of the old town. A heritage article says about 3 kilometres west, on the Thu Bồn, and dates the trade to more than 500 years. It says the village made the yin-yang roof tiles on the old houses. The small red animals in the frame are clay from that village.
No fee and no door hours are printed. Both are check on arrival. This is not the Museum of Trade Ceramics on Trần Phú.

blocks.heading: Kim Bồng wood
paragraphs: Kim Bồng sits on the south bank of the Thu Bồn, opposite the old town. The heritage page dates the village to about the 16th century and names four trades: building wood, household wood, boats, and decorative carving. The carved heads are that last trade. On 21 November 2016 the ministry listed the village as national intangible heritage.
The page says to buy a visit ticket and does not print the price. The crossing from the old town is not printed either. Both are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: The silk village
paragraphs: A 2 May 2018 heritage note recognised Làng lụa Hội An, at 28 Nguyễn Tất Thành, as a local tourism site, on the same list as Kim Bồng and Thanh Hà. The note does not say what the house sells, and it prints no fee and no hour. All three are check on arrival. No licensed photograph of that address was found, so it is not a card.

cards.title: Thanh Hà pottery
cards.summary: Small clay animals from the village about 3 km west of the old town. The old-house tiles are the same trade. The fee and the hours are check on arrival.

cards.title: Kim Bồng carving
cards.summary: Decorative carving, one of the four trades the heritage page names. The visit ticket has no printed price. The river crossing is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Merchant houses
interestGroups.summary: A tube house you can walk, with the shop at the front and the river at the back.

cards.title: Tan Ky House
cards.summary: A tube house at 101 Nguyễn Thái Học, shop at the front and the river at the back. The ground floor is the visit, and the family lives upstairs. Come in the morning. The fee is the ancient-town ticket, which is check on arrival. A visitor page prints a midday close. Confirm that split before you cross town for it.

cards.title: Phung Hung Old House
cards.summary: The timber house at 4 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, more than a hundred years old, with a Chinese balcony, a Japanese four-way roof on the middle bay, and a Vietnamese frame. Eighty ironwood columns stand on stone feet. The eighth generation still lives here. Hours and the fee are check on arrival.

cards.title: Quan Thang Old House
cards.summary: A one-storey merchant house the monument page calls more than 150 years old, opening onto both Trần Phú and Nguyễn Thái Học. Kim Bồng carpenters cut the wood. The sky well is lined with Chinese ceramics. The page does not print the street number, the hours, or a separate fee. All three are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Shop at the front, river at the back
paragraphs: Merchant houses such as Tấn Ký are the inside of the street: a shop at the front and the river at the back. The ground floor is the visit.

interestGroups.title: Assembly halls
interestGroups.summary: The Cantonese hall’s dragon court, the long Fujian hall, and Chùa Ông on Trần Phú.

cards.title: Cantonese Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The Cantonese assembly hall, built in 1885, with a pottery dragon in the court and a hall behind it. It began as a place for Thiên Hậu and Confucius, and after 1911 the worship turned to Quan Công and the earlier merchants. The monument page does not print the street number. Hours and the fee are check on arrival.

cards.title: Fujian Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The long assembly hall at 46 Trần Phú, about 120 metres through three courts to the Thiên Hậu hall. It began in 1697 as Kim Sơn Tự and was rebuilt as the Fujian hall from 1757. Door hours are check on arrival. The fee is the ancient-town ticket, which is also check on arrival.

cards.title: Chaozhou Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The Chaozhou hall at 157 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, also called chùa Âm Bổn, built in 1845 for the community and for the gods of wind and wave. The frame is carved wood, with porcelain reliefs of folk stories. It is a quieter hall than the dragon court. Hours and the fee are check on arrival.

cards.title: Quan Cong Temple
cards.summary: The hall at 24 Trần Phú, built for Quan Công by Minh Hương and Vietnamese residents in the mid-17th century. The main hall holds the statue, two attendants, and two life-size horses. It is a short stop on the Trần Phú walk, and the heavy day is the 16th of the first lunar month. Door hours and the fee are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: The Hoa merchant halls
paragraphs: The assembly halls are the Hoa merchant halls. Quảng Đông is the dragon court. Phúc Kiến is the long hall on Trần Phú. Chùa Ông is at 24 Trần Phú.

interestGroups.title: Museums
interestGroups.summary: Trade ceramics, Sa Huỳnh pottery, and the folk-culture house. A morning hour, not the night.

cards.title: Museum of Trade Ceramics
cards.summary: A nineteenth-century tube house at 80 Trần Phú, opened as a museum in 1995, with 368 ceramics from the 9th to the 19th century. The house itself is the other exhibit: front, bridge, and back, with a sky well. It closes on the 15th of each month. The clock and the fee are check on arrival.

cards.title: Sa Huynh Culture Museum
cards.summary: The museum at 149 Trần Phú for the Sa Huỳnh culture, set up in 1994, with more than a thousand objects from about two thousand years ago and a few from Bãi Ông on Cù Lao Chàm that the overview dates to about three thousand years. It closes on the 10th of each month. The clock and the fee are check on arrival.

cards.title: Museum of Folk Culture
cards.summary: The old house at 33 Nguyễn Thái Học, 57 metres by 9, open as a museum since 24 March 2005. Upstairs are 490 objects on four themes. Downstairs the overview says there are demonstrations. The house runs through to Bạch Đằng. It closes on the 20th of each month. The clock and the fee are check on arrival.

A farmer hour, two shrines, and a stone well are on the heritage page. The fee, the hours, and the ride minutes are check on arrival.

cards.title: Kim Bong Carpentry Village
cards.summary: The carpentry village on the south bank of the Thu Bồn, opposite the old town, in what was Cẩm Kim. The heritage page dates the village to about the 16th century and names four trades: building wood, household wood, boats, and decorative carving. It was listed as national intangible heritage on 21 November 2016. The ticket price and the crossing time are check on arrival.

cards.title: Thanh Ha Pottery Village
cards.summary: The pottery village in khối Nam Diêu, Thanh Hà ward. The craft index puts it 3 kilometres west-southwest of the old town. A heritage article says about 3 kilometres west, on the Thu Bồn, and dates the trade to more than 500 years, with the tiles on the old houses among its work. The fee, the hours, and the ride minutes are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Across the river, and west of town
paragraphs: Kim Bồng is the carpentry village across the river. Thanh Hà is the pottery west of town. Crossing minutes and the ride are check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: An Bang

cards.title: An Bang Beach
cards.summary: Swim or walk the sand from the villa and homestay strip, now in Hoi An Tây. The June 2024 coast article calls that lodging the stay foreign visitors use, and it says erosion threatens this beach as well as Cửa Đại. No entry fee is printed. Chair hire and the ride from the old town are check on arrival.

cards.title: Cam Thanh Coconut Water
cards.summary: Take a basket boat through the nipa water at Cẩm Thanh, about 3 km from the old town on the 2022 heritage article. From 10 August 2026 the entry is 30,000 VND a person. The boat is extra, and that price is check on arrival. Seventeen routes were approved in February 2025. Bad weather can stop the boats.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Hoi An or Da Nang?
faqs.a: Sleep in Hoi An when the timber streets after dark are the reason you came. Sleep in Da Nang when you want the beach in the morning. The ancient town is about 30 km southeast of Da Nang city. The minutes from the airport are check on arrival.

faqs.q: What does the ancient-town ticket cost?
faqs.a: Check on arrival. From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for a Vietnamese and a foreign visitor. The heritage centre’s January and March 2026 notices still describe combination tickets of 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND. A May 2026 article says many people walk the open neighbourhood without a ticket.

faqs.q: Is Hoi An worth visiting in October?
faqs.a: Floods are usual from September to November, and the rainy season on the city climate page runs October to December. The town can be open and under water in the same month. If your dates are fixed, keep a Da Nang hotel as the backup and check the road that morning.

season.label: Flood risk Sep–Nov
season.note: The Da Nang city portal, 4 May 2026, calls January to September dry and October to December the rainy season, with floods usual in September to November and storms mainly September to December. Check the Hoi An road on the morning you go.
